newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels-London Eurostar hits lorry at crossing.
newsitem.headline: Brussels-London Eurostar hits lorry at crossing.

text.p: The driver of an articulated truck had a miracle escape on Tuesday as a high-speed Eurostar passenger train from Brussels to London carved his vehicle in half as he crossed a level crossing in western Belgium.

The train, carrying 100 passengers and travelling at 140 kilometres per hour (90 mph), smashed into the truck as it skidded across the railway line at Ligne, west of Brussels, at around 11.30 a.m.(1030 GMT).
"It is a miracle that no one was hurt," a police spokesman told Reuters Television.
Police said it had been foggy and the driver, who was still in his cab when the train hit, had not seen the stop signals until it was too late.
A Reuters Television crew reported skid marks leading up to the crossing. The two halves of the truck lay on either side of the rail line.
The pointed nose of the train, which had been travelling at the maximum speed allowed on that stretch of line, was smashed and there was extensive damage to the sides of the engine.
The line was blocked for several hours.
An SNCB spokesman said the Brussels London service had been re-routed via Mons and passengers from the train taken by bus to Lille on the Belgian-French border.
